neighbours.label: The closing '."' of a quoted scripture verse before its citation ("... reconciled to God." Ps. 110:1); ordinary closing quotes read lower
fire: The Lord said, "Blessed are they that mourn, for they shall be comforted." Matt. 5:4
We beg you, "Be ye kind one to another, tenderhearted."--Eph. 4:32
He said unto them, "Go ye into all the world, and preach." Mark 16:15
Thus saith the Lord, "I will set my bow in the cloud." Gen. 9:13
And Jesus said, "Let the little children come unto me." Luke 18:16
It is written, "Man shall not live by bread alone."--Matt. 4:4
The psalmist says, "The Lord is my shepherd, I shall not want." Ps. 23:1
"If anyone turns away from My reminder, his life will be narrow..." (Surah Ta Ha, 124)
quiet: The coach said, "Blessed are those who train in the rain, I guess." He laughed.
We beg you, "Be kind to the dog and feed it." She nodded.
He said to them, "Go to the shop and buy some milk." They went.
Thus said the waiter, "I will bring your soup." He left.
And Peter said, "Let the children come to the park." We agreed.
It is said that bread is cheap in this town.
The teacher says, "The class is over, you may go." They rose.
"If anyone calls for me, tell them I am out..." she said.

short: closing quote of a scripture verse
notes: Probes 0.13-0.20, with 0.05 in ordinary speech, so the median is at risk.
